areas.title: Upper Estuary
areas.launchOffset: Opened the day before low tide, then returned to the outer edge for the final flight block
areas.tideWindow: Covered in two separate outer-estuary flights, one well before low tide and one on the returning tide
areas.estimatedDuration: Two outer-estuary flight blocks bracketing the wider survey day
areas.missionRole: Covers the outer estuary and beach-facing edge, giving the baseline survey both its opening seaward context and its closing check back toward the sea.
areas.operationalNote: This area was not captured in one continuous run. It was flown first as Flight 1 and then revisited as Flight 8 after the inner estuary work, which better reflects how the day actually unfolded on site.
areas.deliverables: Orthomosaic, DSM, 3D model, linked sections, future repeat comparison views
areas.weatherNotes: Very good flying conditions with low wind, clear weather, and strong visibility across the open estuary edge.
areas.surveyNotes: This area captures the most open and tidal part of the site. It is important because it records the seaward edge of the estuary, where visible beach-shape and channel-form changes are likely to show up strongly between surveys. In practice, this outer zone was split between the first and last flights of the day rather than covered in one pass.
areas.purpose: Area 1 covers the outer estuary and beach zone, providing the baseline record for the most open and visibly tidal part of the site.

areas.title: Central Estuary
areas.size: Middle reach between the beach and upper estuary
areas.launchOffset: Captured once before the main low-water window and again just ahead of low tide
areas.tideWindow: Covered in two central-estuary flights, both completed before low tide
areas.estimatedDuration: Two central-estuary flights linking the outer and inner coverage
areas.missionRole: Covers the central estuary and links the outer beach zone to the quieter upper reaches, with one early pass and one later pass tying the day together.
areas.operationalNote: This area was not one continuous middle block. It was flown as Flight 2 earlier in the day and Flight 7 later on, so the central reach effectively stitched the outer and inner sequences together.
areas.deliverables: Orthomosaic, DSM, 3D model, linked sections, future repeat comparison views
areas.weatherNotes: Stable conditions continued through this central part of the session, with low wind and no meaningful light or access issues.
areas.surveyNotes: Area 2 acts as the transition zone between the outer estuary and the upper estuary. It is useful because it helps track how exposed surfaces, channel form, and sediment shape change through the middle of the site rather than only at the edges. The flight log shows that this central reach was split across Flights 2 and 7 rather than captured as one long central run.
areas.purpose: Area 2 covers the central estuary, forming the key transition zone between the exposed outer beach area and the calmer upper estuary.

areas.title: Outer Estuary / Beach Zone
areas.size: Upper estuary and mudflat deposition zone
areas.launchOffset: Worked steadily through the middle of the day in the run-up to low tide
areas.tideWindow: Most of the inner estuary was completed in the 105 minutes leading into low tide
areas.estimatedDuration: Four linked inner-estuary flights forming the main mid-session survey block
areas.missionRole: Covers the upper estuary including the quieter mudflat and deposition areas that are likely to be important for repeat monitoring, and forms the main continuous survey block from the day.
areas.operationalNote: This inner-estuary reach was the densest part of the programme, covered through Flights 3, 4, 5, and 6. It was slightly more constrained operationally because of the nearby road and railway line, so flight paths were kept parallel where sensible and then filled in through the middle while maintaining safe separation.
areas.deliverables: Orthomosaic, DSM, 3D model, linked sections, future repeat comparison views
areas.weatherNotes: Conditions remained strong, with low wind and minimal moving water compared with the lower reaches, helping the imagery resolve very clearly.
areas.surveyNotes: This was probably the strongest-performing area because there was less moving water and more stable visible surface detail. It is especially valuable because it shows where sand appears to be depositing onto the mudflats, which is one of the main behaviours the client is interested in tracking.
areas.purpose: Area 3 covers the upper estuary and mudflat reach, where calmer surface conditions and visible deposition make it one of the most important areas for future repeat monitoring.
